charger.title: Charger - sensors
charger.description: The sensors Cable Juice Planner reads from your charger. Status, power and the two kWh meters are required.

data_description.status_entity_id: Charger status (Supported states: on, connect, connected, ready, ready_to_charge, awaiting_authorization, awaiting_start, off, disconnect, disconnected, charging, completed, finished)
data_description.kwh_meter_entity_id: Use Riemann-sum integration sensor (method: Left Riemann-sum) if the charger’s kWh meter is slow (e.g., Easee); otherwise use the charger’s lifetime kWh meter
data_description.lifetime_kwh_meter_entity_id: Alternative to kwh_meter_entity_id if you don’t want to use the charger’s lifetime kWh meter
data_description.enabled_entity_id: Optional: switch/sensor showing if the charger is on (on/off). When the charger is off, the attribute charger_enabled of the action sensor asks to turn it on.
data_description.cable_connected_entity_id: Only used when the charger has no status sensor: tells if the car is connected.

charger_specs.title: Charger - specifications
charger_specs.description: Used to calculate how much can be charged per hour and for the amps sensors.

data_description.charging_phases: Number of phases the car charges with (1-3).
data_description.charging_loss: Charging loss in percent (0 or negative). -5 means 5 % of the energy from the charger is lost. Can be calculated automatically with the Calculate charging loss switch.

load_balancing.title: Load balancing
load_balancing.description:
The place of the car in the shared grid connection.

**Circuit** (chargers sharing one circuit limit):
{circuit}

Only the automation of the master charger sets the circuit limit – see the charger control blueprint.

data.charger_in_phase_meter: Phase sensors include this car's charger

data_description.site_priority: 1 = charges first. A car under the daily minimum or with a trip soon always goes first.
data_description.site_phase_order: Which grid phases the charger L1/L2/L3 are connected to (L2-L3-L1 = charger L1 is house L2). Single phase charging uses charger L1.
data_description.charger_in_phase_meter: On (default): the phase current sensors of the shared grid connection also measure this car's charger. Turn off if the charger is on its own meter that the phase sensors do not include (but behind the same main fuse): its draw is then added to the measured phase current in the overload check and the main fuse check, and is not taken off the measured current to get the house, so the protection is never lower. If you are unsure, let the car charge and watch the phase sensors: if they rise by what it draws, they include it. Turning it off is the safe side for the fuse, but for a charger that the sensors do measure it counts twice: the car then gets less current, and the main fuse repair may appear. Without phase sensors the setting has no effect. Without a reading from the charger's power sensor the car counts with the current it was given.
data_description.site_circuit: Only for chargers sharing one circuit limit (e.g. Easee chargers behind a master). Select this car's charger and the other chargers on the circuit. The selection is shared: the other cars of the circuit get the same change. Leave empty if the charger has its own circuit.

ev.title: EV - sensors (optional)
ev.description: Sensors from the car integration. Without a car integration leave them empty: a virtual battery level that you set is used instead. Battery level, range and odometer must either all be set or all be empty.

data_description.simulate_battery_level_while_charging: Turn on if the car integration is slow to update the battery level (e.g. only every 30–60 minutes). While charging, between the car's updates, CJP lets the battery level rise with the charger's kWh meter, minus the charging loss. Every time the car reports a new battery level (or a new time in Last update), CJP corrects the simulation to the car's value and keeps rising from there. The plan and the charger actions use the simulated level; history, driving efficiency and the charging loss measurement use the car's own value. The simulation stops 1 % below the car's charge limit, so the car itself confirms that the target is reached. The simulated level is shown in Simulated battery level, where you can also enter the car's real value yourself, e.g. when you plug in and the car's value is behind. When you plug in, a notification asks if it matches the car's display. Requires a car integration. Leave it off if the car updates the battery level continuously.
data_description.charge_port_door_entity_id: Indicates port open/closed (Supported states: on, open, plugged, connect, connected, plugged_waiting_for_charge, manual, off, closed, unplugged, disconnect, disconnected)
data_description.charge_cable_entity_id: Indicates if the vehicle is connected (Supported states: on, open, plugged, connect, connected, plugged_waiting_for_charge, manual, off, closed, unplugged, disconnect, disconnected)
data_description.charging_limit_entity_id: Optional: the current charge limit of the car. Used for the charging loss calculation and rounding (Kia/Cupra). The wanted limit is published as the sensor charging_limit. The simulated battery level stops 1 % below it.
data_description.location_entity_id: If not set, falls back to charger.entity_ids.status_entity_id for home/away. Public charging sessions are only detected with a known location
data_description.last_update_entity_id: Optional: time of the last update of the car. No wake_up event when the car updated within 14 minutes. A new time also corrects the simulated battery level.
data_description.climate_entity_id: Optional: the climate entity of the car. Its state tells if preheating runs; start/stop are fired as events on ev_request.

ev_specs.title: EV - battery
ev_specs.description: The battery of the car and how early charging must be done before departure.

data_description.battery_size: Usable battery capacity; verify via OBD2
data_description.last_charging_hour_before_departure_buff: Hours before departure when charging must be completed. If energy is missing, additional charging will be scheduled.

home.title: House consumption
home.description:
Used to calculate the solar surplus that can be used for charging.

Chargers of cars with lower priority found: {cjp_chargers}

data.charger_in_house_meter: House consumption includes this car's charger
data.ignore_cjp_chargers: Ignore chargers of cars with lower priority

data_description.ignore_consumption_from_entity_ids: List of power sensors to ignore
data_description.charger_in_house_meter: On (default): the house consumption sensor also measures this car's charger, so Cable Juice Planner subtracts the charger from it. Turn off if the charger has its own meter that the house consumption sensor does not include, behind the same grid connection as the solar (not a separate connection): the charger is then not subtracted, neither here nor by the cars behind or by BattMind, and the cars behind this one (or with the same priority) add its charging to their house consumption instead, as one meter would. Without a number from the charger power sensor the charger counts with its most. If unsure, leave it on: a repair tells you when the history shows a house consumption under half of what the charger draws.
data_description.ignore_cjp_chargers: Subtracts the charging power of the chargers of your Cable Juice Planner cars with a lower priority (a higher number) from the house consumption, also for cars added later. The car with priority 1 has the first right to the solar surplus, then 2, and so on: this car counts the charging of the cars ahead of it as consumption, but not of the cars behind it. This car's own charger is not included, and a charger that is also in the list above is only subtracted once. Cars with the same priority do not leave each other out. Turn off if your house consumption sensor does not include the chargers.

powerwall.title: Home battery (optional)
powerwall.description: Fill in if you have a home battery. It is used to charge the car from the home battery and to prioritise charging the home battery.

data.powerwall_discharging_power: Home battery discharge power for the car

data_description.powerwall_watt_flow_entity_id: Home battery watt flow (positive = discharging, negative = charging; invert sign with home.invert_powerwall_watt_flow_entity_id). Tip: Disable Powerwall discharging while EV is charging
data_description.powerwall_discharging_power: Home battery discharging power (watts) used to charge the EV when above threshold and switch.PREFIX_powerwall_discharge_above_needed is enabled

detection_review.title: Check the battery and consumption settings
detection_review.description:
Suggested from the recorded history of the battery and house consumption sensors, as far back as needed. Check the numbers – you can change everything.

In the brackets: h = hours of unbroken data, n = battery switch-overs compared, and how far back it was found.

✅ = on, ⬜ = off, ❔ = could not be determined (also when charging and discharging do not point to the same kind of sensor): the current value is kept. Nothing is looked up again while the sensors are unchanged; tick *Detect again* to do it.

**Battery power sign** {invert_mark} ({invert_window})
The battery level went from {soc_start} to {soc_end} % while the average battery power was {power_avg} W. A rising level with positive power means positive = charging: turn *Invert the power sign* on.

**Consumption includes charging** {charging_mark} ({charging_window})
Around the moments the battery started or stopped charging, the house consumption was {c_charging} W while it charged {p_charging} W, against {c_idle_charging} W just before or after, when it was idle. A step of about the charging power means it includes it; no step means it does not.

**Consumption includes discharging** {discharging_mark} ({discharging_window})
Around the moments the battery started or stopped discharging, the house consumption was {c_discharging} W while it discharged {p_discharging} W, against {c_idle_discharging} W just before or after, when it was idle. A fall of about the discharge power means it does not include it; no fall means it does (if the house uses at least as much as the battery gives).

data_description.invert_powerwall_watt_flow_entity_id: Invert sign for home.entity_ids.powerwall_watt_flow_entity_id (charging positive, discharging negative)
data_description.power_consumption_entity_id_include_powe: Home consumption incl. home battery charging (watts)
Home consumption incl. home battery discharging (watts)
data_description.redetect: Looks at the recorder again for the three sensors and puts what it finds in the settings above. Nothing is saved until you continue without it.

prices_energidataservice.title: Energi Data Service
prices_energidataservice.description: Sensors of the [Energi Data Service]({eds_url}) integration. Enable Carnot (AI price forecast) to plan beyond the published prices.

prices_stromligning.title: Strømligning

prices_stromligning_tariffs.title: Strømligning - tariffs when selling

price_fees.title: Refund and fees
price_fees.description: Amounts per kWh that change what charging and selling solar is worth.

solar.title: Solar panels (optional)
solar.description:
Fill in if you have solar panels. The surplus is used to charge the car and the forecast is used in the plan.

Forecast.Solar and Helios Forecast are read from their solar forecast for the Energy dashboard; the hours they don't cover are planned from the weather forecast and the stored solar history; an hour with neither counts as no sun.

Solcast switches the forecast sensors of day 3 and on off by default: enable them under **Settings → Devices & services → Entities** (*Show disabled entities*) and turn on *Hourly detail* under *Forecast attributes breakdown* in the Solcast options, or those days are planned without Solcast.
Disabled Solcast sensors now: {solcast_disabled}

data_description.forecast_entity_id: Solcast PV Forecast, Forecast.Solar or Helios Forecast. Solcast: e.g. sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_today, the days ahead are found automatically. Forecast.Solar: any of its sensors; the roof planes of the same solar source in the Energy dashboard are added up. Helios Forecast: e.g. sensor.helios_forecast_power_now.
data_description.enable_selling_during_expensive_hours: Enable selling during expensive hours; if disabled, solar goes to EV charging. “Fixed solar sell price” must be −1.0 to use spot price
data_description.solar_sell_fixed_price: Fixed sell price for solar, used to calculate solar surplus. Set to -1.0 to use the hourly spot price.

solar_charging.title: Solar charging
solar_charging.description: How the solar surplus is turned into charging current.

data.max_to_current_hour: Use the surplus within the hour

data_description.solarpower_use_before_minutes: Number of minutes you can ’borrow’ against expected solar surplus
data_description.max_to_current_hour: Require use of surplus within the current hour
data_description.allow_grid_charging_above_solar_availabl: Allowed difference in watts above(+)/below(−) surplus
data_description.charging_single_phase_min_amp: Minimum current on 1-phase; set 0 to disable
data_description.charging_single_phase_max_amp: Maximum current on 1-phase; set 0 to disable

weather.title: Weather
weather.description: The weather forecast is used to predict the solar surplus (with solar), for preheating and for the “Adjust driving efficiency to temperature” switch. The page can be filled in without solar too.

data_description.outdoor_temp_entity_id: Used for preheat/defrost decisions with more accurate temperature than forecast, and gives the drives under Analysis their outdoor temperature

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Who gets notifications from Cable Juice Planner and which ones.

data.notify_charger_offline: Charger not responding before a departure
data.notify_cheap_power: Cheap power, car not plugged in
data.notify_manual_expensive: Manual charging in an expensive hour
data.notify_battery_full: Battery full for a long time

data_description.notify_list: notify services that get the CJP notifications (e.g. notify.mobile_app_phone). Empty = notify.notify. Use mobile_app for actionable notifications.
data_description.efficiency_on_cable_plug_in: Notify last drive efficiency on cable plug-in
data_description.departure_readiness: Notify once per departure when the car will not be ready for the next departure (within 24 hours): too few charging hours, a need above the charge limit, the car's own charge limit too low (already at plug-in when the charger automation does not set it), the car stopping charging early, or charging much slower than planned. Also when charging planned for it starts within an hour while the car is home but not plugged in.
data_description.notify_charger_offline: Notify once per departure when the charger's status has been unavailable or unknown for 30 minutes while charging for a departure within 24 hours is planned.
data_description.notify_cheap_power: Notify at most once a day when charging at a very cheap price or a price below 0 is planned within the hour, and the car is home but not plugged in. Not for the charging a departure needs (Car not ready / plug in covers that).
data_description.notify_manual_expensive: Notify at most once a day when manual charging is on and the car charges in one of the day's 4 most expensive hours.
data_description.notify_monthly_summary: Notify once a month with last month's charged kWh, cost, average price and the saving compared with daily charging. Not for a month CJP did not see from its start or without a known cost.
data_description.notify_site_limit: Notify when load balancing (the main fuse or the site limit) has stopped or lowered the charging of the plugged-in car for two check intervals and at least 10 minutes, each at most once a day. Not during the charger test.
data_description.notify_battery_full: Notify when the car's own battery level has stood at 99 % or more for 12 hours (24 hours when a full charge every X days is set or not known), once per time it is full. Again after 30 days if it is still full. Needs the car integration.
data_description.notify_charging_loss: Notify at most once a month when the kWh per 1 % at 4 kW or more over the last 30 days is at least 15 % above 3–6 months ago, with enough measurements in both, and also above the same months a year earlier when they have enough measurements. Cold weather raises it too.

data_description.cron_interval: Minutes between each check of the plan and the charging.
data_description.dashboard: Adds a ready-made Cable Juice Planner dashboard to the sidebar for this instance. Needs the HACS cards mushroom, apexcharts-card, config-template-card and card-mod (optional). A notification lists missing cards.
data_description.enable_diagnostic_file_log: Writes a detailed log to cable_juice_planner_PREFIX.log in the config folder (2 MB per file, 3 rotations).

data_description.power_values_db_data_to_save: Number of days of power values to retain
data_description.solar_available_db_data_to_save: Amount stored per cloud cover category
data_description.charging_history_db_data_to_save: Keep X months of charging history

price_provider.title: Electricity prices
price_provider.description: Choose where the hourly prices come from. With both, Strømligning has priority: its price is used for every hour it has one, and Energi Data Service fills the gaps.

instance.title: Add EV / charger
instance.description: Cable Juice Planner plans when the EV should charge from electricity prices, driving, solar forecast and home battery. The integration sends no commands to the charger or the car: the plan and the actions are published as entities (e.g. `sensor.cjp_‹prefix›_charger_action` and the amps sensors) that you use in your own automations.

data_description.name: Optional, e.g. Tesla or Family car. Used as the device name (entities show as e.g. Tesla Overview) and in the notifications.
data_description.entity_prefix: Optional. All entities start with cjp_, the prefix follows: tesla gives sensor.cjp_tesla_overview, empty gives sensor.cjp_overview. Use a different prefix for each car. Cannot be changed later.
data_description.language: Language of the entity names, the overview, the charging history, the charging rule and notifications.
data_description.dashboard_icon: Icon of the dashboard in the sidebar, e.g. mdi:ev-station. Leave empty for the default icon.

site.title: Shared grid connection
site.description: Load balancing between several cars: the cars are planned by priority, so together they never use more current per phase than the main fuse. A car with lower priority charges with fewer amps or in other hours.

data_description.fuse_l1: The main fuse (or the limit the cars may use together) per phase.
data_description.fuse_l2: The main fuse (or the limit the cars may use together) per phase.
data_description.fuse_l3: The main fuse (or the limit the cars may use together) per phase.
data_description.margin: Subtracted from the fuse to leave room for short peaks.
data_description.voltage: Used when the phase sensors measure power (W, kW …) instead of current (A).
data_description.phase_l1_entity_id: Optional: measured current (A or mA) or power (W, kW, mW, MW or GW) per phase of the whole house (e.g. a HAN/P1 meter). A sensor in an energy unit (Wh, kWh) can't be used: it doesn't show the current right now. With all three the house consumption is subtracted. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars, and each car's charging power sensor shows what it really draws. Either way an overloaded phase limits the last car at once.
data_description.phase_l2_entity_id: Optional: measured current (A or mA) or power (W, kW, mW, MW or GW) per phase of the whole house (e.g. a HAN/P1 meter). A sensor in an energy unit (Wh, kWh) can't be used: it doesn't show the current right now. With all three the house consumption is subtracted. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars, and each car's charging power sensor shows what it really draws. Either way an overloaded phase limits the last car at once.
data_description.phase_l3_entity_id: Optional: measured current (A or mA) or power (W, kW, mW, MW or GW) per phase of the whole house (e.g. a HAN/P1 meter). A sensor in an energy unit (Wh, kWh) can't be used: it doesn't show the current right now. With all three the house consumption is subtracted. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars, and each car's charging power sensor shows what it really draws. Either way an overloaded phase limits the last car at once.
data_description.urgent_trip_hours: A planned trip within this many hours gives the car precedence.

import_legacy.title: Import from the PyScript version

restore_backup.title: Restore from a backup
restore_backup.description:
Cable Juice Planner backups found in **cable_juice_planner_backups** (written by Export data and when a Cable Juice Planner device is deleted).

Choose one to restore it as **{prefix}**: its configuration is used as defaults on the next pages, and the databases and settings are restored on first start.

error.detection_recorder: The suggestions could not be made: the recorder is not running, so there is no history. The current values are kept.
error.detection_timeout: Reading the history took too long. The current values are kept; tick *Detect again* to try again.
error.detection_error: The history could not be read. The current values are kept; tick *Detect again* to try again.
error.detection_data: The sensors have no usable history (or it is too short). The current values are kept.
error.detection_unit: A power sensor has an unknown unit (not W, kW …), so the history can't be compared. The current values are kept.
error.invalid_prefix: Use 1-50 lower case letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter.
error.prefix_in_use: This prefix is already used by another Cable Juice Planner instance.
error.prefix_entities_exist: Entities with this prefix already exist (e.g. from the PyScript version). Choose another prefix or remove the old entities.
error.no_price_provider: Choose at least one price provider.
error.production_required: A solar forecast needs a solar production sensor.
error.ev_incomplete: Battery level, range and odometer must all be set (or all be empty).
error.simulation_needs_ev: Simulating the battery level requires the car's battery level, range and odometer.
error.min_above_max: The minimum cannot be above the maximum.
error.invalid_icon: Use an icon name like mdi:ev-station.
error.circuit_no_charger_device: The car's charger entities belong to no device, so the charger cannot be linked to a circuit.
error.circuit_own_charger_missing: Select this car's charger as well.

abort.site_exists: A shared grid connection already exists.

Turn off if your house consumption sensor does not include the chargers.

powerwall.title: Home battery (optional)
powerwall.description: Fill in if you have a home battery. It is used to charge the car from the home battery and to prioritise charging the home battery.

data.powerwall_discharging_power: Home battery discharge power for the car

detection_review.title: Check the battery and consumption settings
detection_review.description:
Suggested from the recorded history of the battery and house consumption sensors, as far back as needed. Check the numbers – you can change everything.

In the brackets: h = hours of unbroken data, n = battery switch-overs compared, and how far back it was found.

✅ = on, ⬜ = off, ❔ = could not be determined (also when charging and discharging do not point to the same kind of sensor): the current value is kept. Nothing is looked up again while the sensors are unchanged; tick *Detect again* to do it.

**Battery power sign** {invert_mark} ({invert_window})
The battery level went from {soc_start} to {soc_end} % while the average battery power was {power_avg} W. A rising level with positive power means positive = charging: turn *Invert the power sign* on.

**Consumption includes charging** {charging_mark} ({charging_window})
Around the moments the battery started or stopped charging, the house consumption was {c_charging} W while it charged {p_charging} W, against {c_idle_charging} W just before or after, when it was idle. A step of about the charging power means it includes it; no step means it does not.

**Consumption includes discharging** {discharging_mark} ({discharging_window})
Around the moments the battery started or stopped discharging, the house consumption was {c_discharging} W while it discharged {p_discharging} W, against {c_idle_discharging} W just before or after, when it was idle. A fall of about the discharge power means it does not include it; no fall means it does (if the house uses at least as much as the battery gives).

Home consumption incl. home battery discharging (watts)

solar.title: Solar panels (optional)
solar.description:
Fill in if you have solar panels. The surplus is used to charge the car and the forecast is used in the plan.

Forecast.Solar and Helios Forecast are read from their solar forecast for the Energy dashboard; the hours they don't cover are planned from the weather forecast and the stored solar history; an hour with neither counts as no sun.

Solcast switches the forecast sensors of day 3 and on off by default: enable them under **Settings → Devices & services → Entities** (*Show disabled entities*) and turn on *Hourly detail* under *Forecast attributes breakdown* in the Solcast options, or those days are planned without Solcast.
Disabled Solcast sensors now: {solcast_disabled}

data_description.forecast_entity_id: Solcast PV Forecast, Forecast.Solar or Helios Forecast. Solcast: e.g. sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_today, the days ahead are found automatically. Forecast.Solar: any of its sensors; the roof planes of the same solar source in the Energy dashboard are added up. Helios Forecast: e.g. sensor.helios_forecast_power_now.

data_description.departure_readiness: Notify once per departure when the car will not be ready for the next departure (within 24 hours): too few charging hours, a need above the charge limit, the car's own charge limit too low (already at plug-in when the charger automation does not set it), the car stopping charging early, or charging much slower than planned. data_description.notify_manual_expensive: Notify at most once a day when manual charging is on and the car charges in one of the day's 4 most expensive hours.
data_description.notify_monthly_summary: Notify once a month with last month's charged kWh, cost, average price and the saving compared with daily charging. Not for a month CJP did not see from its start or without a known cost.
data_description.notify_site_limit: Notify when load balancing (the main fuse or the site limit) has stopped or lowered the charging of the plugged-in car for two check intervals and at least 10 minutes, each at most once a day. Not during the charger test.

Cold weather raises it too.

site.description: Load balancing between several cars: the cars are planned by priority, so together they never use more current per phase than the main fuse. A car with lower priority charges with fewer amps or in other hours.

data_description.phase_l1_entity_id: Optional: measured current (A or mA) or power (W, kW, mW, MW or GW) per phase of the whole house (e.g. a HAN/P1 meter). A sensor in an energy unit (Wh, kWh) can't be used: it doesn't show the current right now. With all three the house consumption is subtracted. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars, and each car's charging power sensor shows what it really draws. Either way an overloaded phase limits the last car at once.

A sensor in an energy unit (Wh, kWh) can't be used: it doesn't show the current right now. With all three the house consumption is subtracted. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars, and each car's charging power sensor shows what it really draws. Either way an overloaded phase limits the last car at once.

A sensor in an energy unit (Wh, kWh) can't be used: it doesn't show the current right now. With all three the house consumption is subtracted. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars, and each car's charging power sensor shows what it really draws. Either way an overloaded phase limits the last car at once.

backup.title: Backup
backup.description:
Export writes the databases, settings and configuration to a file in **cable_juice_planner_backups**.

Importing a file replaces the databases and settings of **{prefix}** with the backup (the current data is exported first, as a *_before_import* file) and reloads the integration.

data_description.restore_configuration: Use the entities and options of the backup as well. Leave off when the backup comes from another Home Assistant.

error.detection_recorder: The suggestions could not be made: the recorder is not running, so there is no history. The current values are kept.

error.detection_data: The sensors have no usable history (or it is too short). The current values are kept.

error.invalid_prefix: Use 1-50 lower case letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter.
error.prefix_in_use: This prefix is already used by another Cable Juice Planner instance.
error.prefix_entities_exist: Entities with this prefix already exist (e.g. from the PyScript version). Choose another prefix or remove the old entities.
error.no_price_provider: Choose at least one price provider.

error.ev_incomplete: Battery level, range and odometer must all be set (or all be empty).
error.simulation_needs_ev: Simulating the battery level requires the car's battery level, range and odometer.
error.min_above_max: The minimum cannot be above the maximum.
error.invalid_icon: Use an icon name like mdi:ev-station.

blueprint_single_entity_inputs.title: Select the entities in the charger control automations again
blueprint_single_entity_inputs.description:
These automations use the blueprint **Cable Juice Planner - charger control** with a single entity in *Status or "charging" entities* / *Charging power*:

{automations}

They still work. These fields take several entities now, and the automation editor shows a single entity there as empty, so saving the automation without selecting it again removes it. Open each automation, select the entities again and save.

The repair disappears when no automation has a single entity left.

confirm.title: Update the blueprint {name}
confirm.description:
Cable Juice Planner comes with a version of the blueprint **{name}** that differs from `{path}`.

Select **Submit** to replace the file with the bundled version and reload the automations that use it. Changes you made to the file yourself are overwritten – copy it to another file name first if you want to keep them.

Ignore this repair to keep your own file.

voltage_old_default.title: The grid voltage of {name} is the old default {voltage} V

confirm.title: Set the grid voltage of {name} to {default} V
confirm.description:
The grid voltage of **{name}** (under *Charger - specifications* in the options) is {voltage} V, the default of earlier versions of Cable Juice Planner. The default is now {default} V, the nominal voltage in most of Europe. CJP counts the charging power of the plan and of the solar steps with it, and turns the charger's measured power into amps for the load balancing: a voltage set too high counts a car's current too low.

Select **Submit** to set it to {default} V (the entry is reloaded). If your grid really has {voltage} V, ignore this repair. You can change the voltage at any time in the options.

stromligning_entities.title: Strømligning sensors that Cable Juice Planner needs are not available ({prefix})

solcast_entities.title: Solcast forecast sensors that Cable Juice Planner needs are not available ({prefix})

entities_missing.title: Entities of Cable Juice Planner ({prefix}) are disabled or missing

entity_units.title: Sensors with a unit Cable Juice Planner can't read ({prefix})
entity_units.description:
Cable Juice Planner ({prefix}) reads these sensors in a fixed unit. Their unit is another one, so the code reads their values as if they were in an accepted unit, and the values are wrong:
{entities}

Accepted units: power sensors {power_units} (a unit with an h, such as Wh or kWh, is read as the unit without it; a power sensor without a unit is read as W); battery level sensors %; kWh meters only in {energy_units}. While the repair to update the charger blueprint is open, the charger power sensor is only read right in W or kW.

Change the unit in the integration that provides the sensor, or pick another sensor. Then run the charger test: turn on **Test my charger automation** under *Settings* on the dashboard. This repair disappears by itself when every sensor has an accepted unit again.

site_phase_units.title: Phase sensors in an energy unit (load balancing)
site_phase_units.description:
These phase sensors report an energy (such as Wh or kWh), not a current or a power:
{entities}

An energy meter can't tell how much current flows on the phase right now, so load balancing doesn't read these sensors. Until they are fixed, the house's consumption is counted as its last measurement or the forecast, or as the whole budget without either: then the cars get no current until the sensors are fixed. The last measurement and the forecast are only an estimate: if the house uses more than that, the main fuse is not protected by a measurement, and otherwise the cars may get less current than they could. The house forecast isn't updated either.

Pick a sensor in A, W or kW for each phase in the settings of the shared grid connection. The repair disappears by itself when no phase sensor reports an energy any more.

blueprint_automation_lost.title: The charger automation of Cable Juice Planner ({prefix}) is disabled or gone
blueprint_automation_lost.description:
The automation made from the Cable Juice Planner charger blueprint was running before, but now it is disabled or no longer in automations.yaml. Without it the charger does not get the actions of the plan.

Disabled:
{automations}

When the list shows –, the automation was deleted.

Turn the automation on again under **Settings → Automations & scenes**, or make it again from the blueprint. Then run the charger test: turn on **Test my charger automation** under *Settings* on the dashboard. This repair disappears by itself when the automation runs again.

charger_status_unknown.title: The charger status is a value Cable Juice Planner does not know ({prefix})
charger_status_unknown.description:
The status of the charger has been one of these values for at least {minutes} minutes. Cable Juice Planner does not know them: they are neither a ready, not ready, charging, completed nor error status. The last time each was seen is shown:
{values}

While the status has such a value, the plan goes on as if the charger were ready. Cable Juice Planner does not restart a charger that does not charge, does not see a car being plugged in (so manual and forced charging are not reset and the car is not woken up), does not count the charger's kWh meter for the battery level simulation, and counts the charger as charging in the load balancing.

If the value is a normal status of your charger, report it with **Export debug info** on the device. Otherwise check the charger integration. Then run the charger test: turn on **Test my charger automation** under *Settings* on the dashboard. This repair disappears by itself when no such value has been seen for {days} days.

power_without_unit.title: Power sensors without a unit are read as W ({prefix})
power_without_unit.description:
Cable Juice Planner ({prefix}) reads these power sensors in watts (W), because they have no unit:
{entities}

The number after ≤ is the highest value seen (without sign).

Over the last {days} days their values never went above {max}, and some of them are decimal numbers, so they look like kilowatts (kW). Read as W they are 1000 times too small, and the plan uses far too little power.

Fix it at the sensor: give it its unit, for example `unit_of_measurement: kW` on a template sensor, or the unit that its integration provides. If the values really are watts, choose **Ignore** on this repair. This repair disappears by itself once the sensors have a unit, or their values show that they are watts.

battery_level_fraction.title: Battery levels that look like a share, not a percentage ({prefix})
battery_level_fraction.description:
Cable Juice Planner ({prefix}) reads these battery levels as percent:
{entities}

The number after ≤ is the highest value seen (without sign).

Over the last {days} days every value of these sensors was between 0 and 1, so they look like a share (0.85 means 85 %). Read as percent, 0.85 is 0.85 %, so the plan works with a battery level that is 100 times too low.

Fix it at the sensor: make it report 0 to 100, for example by multiplying by 100 in a template sensor, and select that sensor in the settings. If the values really are percent and only happen to be below 1, choose **Ignore** on this repair. This repair disappears by itself once the sensors report 0 to 100, or their values show percent.

price_unit_scale.title: Price sensors in a subunit, per MWh or per Wh ({prefix})
price_unit_scale.description:
Cable Juice Planner ({prefix}) reads these price sensors as prices per kWh in the currency, but their unit is a subunit of the currency (øre or cent), per MWh or per Wh:
{entities}

No price is converted, so the prices are 100 or 1000 times too large (subunit, per MWh) or 1000 times too small (per Wh), and the plan and the savings calculation are wrong. Only the unit is judged, not the size of the prices.

Fix it at the source: in Energi Data Service turn off **Show prices in cent** and set **Price calculated in** to kWh in the options of the integration, or select a sensor whose unit is the currency per kWh (e.g. kr/kWh). If the unit really is correct, choose **Ignore** on this repair. This repair disappears by itself once every price sensor is in the currency per kWh (e.g. kr/kWh).

consumption_frozen.title: House consumption sensor shows the same value for 6 hours ({prefix})
consumption_frozen.description:
Cable Juice Planner ({prefix}) uses the house consumption sensor {entity} for the house consumption in the plan. It has shown {value} since {since}: at least 6 hours without a change.

The plan uses this sensor for the house, so a sensor that stays the same gives it a wrong house consumption. Check the integration or the device that delivers the sensor: it may have stopped sending values. If the value really is constant, choose **Ignore** on this repair.

This repair disappears by itself once the sensor reports a different value. An unavailable sensor keeps the repair as it is. The planner's notification about an unavailable sensor only covers a sensor with an entity registry entry (for example from an integration, made in the UI, or YAML with a unique ID).

charger_outside_house_meter.title: The house consumption does not seem to include the charger ({prefix})
charger_outside_house_meter.description:
Cable Juice Planner ({prefix}) subtracts this car's charger from the house consumption sensor {entity}, because the setting **House consumption includes this car's charger** is on. But in {hours} hours of the last {days} days the house consumption was under {share} % of what the charger alone drew, without solar and without the home battery charging or discharging. A sensor that includes the charger can never be lower than the charger, so the charger is probably on its own meter. The charger is then subtracted from a house that never had it: the house consumption becomes too low, and the plan sees solar surplus and cheap hours that are not there.

If the charger is on its own meter, turn off **House consumption includes this car's charger** in the options of this car (the House consumption page). If the house consumption sensor should include the charger, check the sensor. If the values are right as they are, choose **Ignore** on this repair.

This repair disappears by itself when the setting is turned off, when the house consumption sensor or the charger power sensor is removed, or when the hours of the last {days} days show that the house consumption includes the charger.

site_fuse_exceeded.title: The house and the cars draw more than the main fuse (load balancing)
site_fuse_exceeded.description:
In the last {days} days the hourly mean current on these phases was above {factor} times the main fuse for {hours} hours or more. Each line shows the phase, its main fuse → the highest hourly mean current (hours above the limit > the limit, which is the main fuse times {factor}):
{phases}

A fuse of that size is unlikely to carry such a current for an hour. So either the main fuse on the shared grid connection page is set too low (the cars then get less current than they could), or a charger that the phase sensors do measure is set as outside them (*Phase sensors include this car's charger* turned off), so its draw is counted twice, or a phase sensor measures something else: phases in the wrong order, a sensor that is not the grid phase, or a wrong unit. Check the fuse size and the phase sensors. If the fuse really is that large and the values are correct, choose **Ignore** on this repair.

This repair disappears by itself when the next forecast no longer finds it: after the fuse is corrected, at the latest when these hours are out of the last {days} days.

charger_not_following.title: The charger did not follow the plan {count} times in {days} days ({prefix})
charger_not_following.description:
In the last {days} days the charger did not follow the plan {count} times. This repair appears at {limit} times or more. The restarts of the charger gave up {gave_up} times, and the charger charged without a rule {no_rule} times. Each of these had its own notification.

Latest events (local time):
{latest}

Check the integration of the charger and the car (does the charger report its status and power?), and any other app or automation that controls the charger or the car: it may stop or start it. Then run the charger test: turn on **Test my charger automation** under *Settings* on the dashboard. This repair disappears by itself when fewer than {limit} of these events are left within {days} days.
